cards.hook: A Tuesday reckoning in French Polynesia changed the whole tone of the week.

cards.body: The week carried forward the energy of March 8 — tennis, a run, weights, Gremly progress, all before sunset in Bora Bora. But the more important thing happened a few days later: a quiet, honest moment of choosing Dave over the app. Not dramatic. Just real.
cards.quote: Felt very very refreshed this morning. Very grateful to be here with Dave and so happy we have another week.
cards.headline: Paradise, with your eyes open

moments.body: It didn't come from a bad day — it came from a great one. Somewhere between the lagoon and the laptop, something clicked: the app would still be there. This moment on the water with Dave wouldn't. Naming that out loud, even just in a journal, was the week's most important act.
moments.title: The honest reckoning

moments.body: A sunburn you didn't mind. Hours on the water with Dave, untethered from screens or schedules. The kind of uncomplicated joy that's hard to manufacture and easy to miss if you're not paying attention — and this week, you were paying attention.
moments.title: Vitamin D and floatie time

spotlight.title: Your clearest thinking arrives on your best days
spotlight.takeaway: The March 12 reflection didn't come from struggle — it came after a day of tennis, running, and real progress. Your wisdom surfaces when you're already winning.
spotlight.evidence_trail: March 8: tennis, run, weights, Gremly progress, no alcohol — your most productive honeymoon day. March 12, just days later: the clearest-eyed self-assessment of the trip. Compare this to pre-travel weeks (Feb 23–26) where anxiety and guilt dominated despite similar workloads. The pattern holds: compression weeks produce anxiety; momentum days produce insight.

research_context.body: Broaden-and-build theory (Fredrickson, 2001) suggests positive emotions expand cognitive range, enabling meta-awareness that produces genuine self-insight.
